f.title: Have a QPPV resident in Ghana permanently and continuously available
f.statement: The MAH shall permanently and continuously have at its disposal an appropriately qualified person responsible for pharmacovigilance (QPPV), who shall be resident in Ghana.
f.applicability: MAHs/manufacturers and Local Representatives of products with marketing authorization in Ghana (FDA Guideline on QPPV, FDA/SMD/GDL-03/07)

f.title: Give the QPPV sufficient authority over PV activities, RMP input and safety regulatory actions
f.statement: The MAH should ensure that the QPPV has sufficient authority to implement pharmacovigilance activities, provide input into the Risk Management Plan when necessary, and provide input into regulatory documents responding to emerging safety concerns (e.g. variations, urgent safety restrictions and, as appropriate, communication to patients and healthcare professionals).

f.statement: The MAH should ensure that appropriate processes, resources, communication mechanisms and access to all sources of relevant information are in place for the QPPV to fulfil his or her responsibilities and tasks.

f.title: Submit QPPV information to FDA: CV, contacts, responsibilities, back-up and delegated tasks
f.statement: The MAH shall submit to the Authority, for the QPPV: a CV with key information on the QPPV role; contact details (name, telephone, fax, e-mail, postal and official working address); a description of responsibilities guaranteeing sufficient authority over the PV system; details of back-up arrangements for the QPPV's absence; and a list of tasks delegated by the QPPV and to whom.

rows.quote: The MAH shall submit the following information to the Authority relating to the qualified person responsible for pharmacovigilance a. curriculum vitae including key information on the role of the qualified person responsible for pharmacovigilance b. contact details including but not limited to the name, telephone, fax and e-mail, postal and official working address c. a description of the responsibilities guaranteeing that the QPPV has sufficient authority over the pharmacovigilance system in order to promote, maintain and improve compliance; d. details of back-up arrangements to apply in the absence of the qualified person responsible for pharmacovigilance; and e. a list of tasks that have been delegated by the qualified person for pharmacovigilance and to whom these tasks have been delegated.

f.title: QPPV and back-up QPPV should know Ghanaian PV law and the MAH's PV system
f.statement: The QPPV and the back-up QPPV should have knowledge of applicable Ghanaian safety monitoring legislation and guidelines and international PV standards, and demonstrate (e.g. through qualifications and training) knowledge of the key PV activities of the MAH's PV system and how to implement them.
f.applicability: MAHs/manufacturers and Local Representatives of products with marketing authorization in Ghana (FDA Guideline on QPPV, FDA/SMD/GDL-03/07)

f.title: QPPV designation lasts three years; apply for re-designation with evidence of conditions
f.statement: The QPPV is eligible to perform the assigned responsibilities for three years after completing the formal training. The FDA re-designates the QPPV for another three years on application (Appendix II) with evidence of: no pending CAPA after a GVP inspection; good standing in the professional body; and participation in at least one PV conference or patient-safety training programme, or passing an FDA written exam on QPPV roles.
f.applicability: MAHs/manufacturers and Local Representatives of products with marketing authorization in Ghana (FDA Guideline on QPPV, FDA/SMD/GDL-03/07)

rows.quote: The QPPV shall be eligible for the performance of the responsibilities assigned for a period of three (3) years after successfully completing the training programme described in Section 3.3.1 (iii) ii. The FDA shall re-designate the QPPV for another three years upon application (Refer Appendix II) and evidence of the underlisted conditions. iii. No pending Corrective and Preventive Action Plan (CAPA) after a GVP Inspection. iv. Good standing in the professional body/association the QPPV belongs to (e.g. Ghana Medical Association, Pharmaceutical Society of Ghana, etc). v. Participation in at least one pharmacovigilance conference OR training programme relevant to patient safety OR passing a written exam related to the QPPV roles administered by the Food and Drugs Authority.
rows.review_note: Review: quote, statement, actor and level checked against the source; no change. Double-check: quote verbatim; level follows the source modal; statement adds nothing beyond the quote.

f.title: QPPV is the single point of contact for FDA on PV, including inspections
f.statement: The QPPV shall act as the single point of contact for the Authority on all matters relating to pharmacovigilance and safety of marketed products, including pharmacovigilance inspections, and shall serve as point of contact and be available during inspections.

f.title: QPPV establishes a system to collect, process and forward all suspected ADRs within timelines
f.statement: The QPPV shall establish and maintain a system ensuring that information on all suspected ADRs/events reported to MAH personnel, including medical representatives, is collected, collated, processed, evaluated and forwarded to the Authority within the timelines it stipulates.
f.applicability: MAHs/manufacturers and Local Representatives of products with marketing authorization in Ghana (FDA Guideline on QPPV, FDA/SMD/GDL-03/07)

f.title: QPPV prepares ADR reports, PSURs/PBRERs, study reports, RMPs and ongoing PV evaluations
f.statement: The QPPV shall prepare for submission to the Authority: ADR reports; PSURs/PBRERs when necessary; company-sponsored pre- and post-registration study reports; Risk Management Plans and Ghana-specific RMPs when requested; and ongoing pharmacovigilance evaluation during the post-registration period.

f.statement: All RMPs submitted shall be accompanied by a declaration signed by the QPPV (Appendix III) stating that the QPPV has read the RMP and will ensure implementation of all activities outlined in it.

f.title: Non-compliance with QPPV requirements leads to sanctions up to revocation
f.statement: Regulatory sanctions shall be applied to the Local Representative or manufacturer for non-compliance with this guideline: notification and advice, formal warning, blacklisting, publication of seriously or persistently non-compliant companies, urgent safety restriction, and variation, suspension or revocation of the marketing authorization; penalties follow Public Health Act 2012 sections 142 and 148.
